arxiv-2605-09239: Ask a model to count repeated tokens and something odd appears: what it represents internally dissociates from what it outputs. Sohan Venkatesh uses this simple task to reveal the gap between representations and outputs. The 2026 paper is a crisp experiment in interpretability.
arxiv-2605-09439: Matching a conditional distribution — generating the right outputs for each input — can be framed as inverse design. arxiv-2605-09939: Tractor-trailers are notoriously hard to navigate — the trailer follows its own mind; neural distance-guided path integral control steers them. Peng Wei, Chen Peng, and Stavros Vougioukas develop the controller. The 2026 paper is robotics for the humble big rig.
plos-pone-0003439: Developmental biologists caught the machinery of embryo folding in this 2008 study. plos-pone-0003539: Motor-control researchers showed hands know what minds forget in this 2008 study. plos-pone-0003639: In 2008, a team asked if years of schooling track with cancer risk in the United States. They followed a large group of men and women and compared cancer rates by level of school done. The data show how far a social factor can reach into who gets cancer and who stays clear.
plos-pone-0003739: In 2008, Manirarora, Kosiewicz, and Parnell restored peacekeeper cells in diabetic mice. plos-pone-0003839: A 2008 genomics study hunted parent-stamped genes in newborn mouse brains. plos-pone-0003939: In 2008, Andrew Gallagher tested claims of tiny ancient humans on Palau. Bones found on the Micronesian islands were said to show island dwarfism in people. His statistical analysis asked whether the size variation really supports a small-bodied population claim.
plos-pone-0004039: In 2008, Murray, Hackett, and Warner tested a hoped-for anti-scarring protein. BMP-7 failed to protect mice against bleomycin-induced lung or skin fibrosis. plos-pone-0004139: In 2009, Kumar, Farhana, and Hasnain watched TB's genome unzip in a dish. DnaA pried open the M. tuberculosis origin helix at a precise spot. The IciA protein blocked the opening. The start-gun mechanics expose a target for stalling TB replication.
plos-pone-0004239: In 2009, Xu, Shi, and Chen traced immune weapon evolution in Asian bees. Antimicrobial peptides in the Asiatic honey bee Apis cerana showed a dynamic history. The bee's defense molecules evolved fast under pressure. The study enriches insect immunity research greatly.
plos-pone-0004339: In 2009, Asrar, Zhou, and Ren mapped a key memory switch's wiring. Calcium-permeable AMPA receptors drove potentiation via PI3/MAP kinases alone. plos-pone-0358839: Peste des petits ruminants is a fast-moving viral disease that kills sheep and goats across Africa and Asia. This study infected goats with the virus in a controlled experiment to measure how quickly it passes from animal to animal. plos-pone-0340539: Paying small farmers to protect rainforest sounds like a fix for deforestation, and this study put the idea to the test in the Colombian Amazon. The paper lays out what worked, what fell short, and what stronger policies would be needed for conservation payments to truly save the Amazon’s trees.
plos-pone-0358539: Psychiatric patients often take a risky cocktail of drugs. plos-pone-0358239: Drug nanocarriers must be swallowed by immune cells to work — and electrostatics govern the uptake. plos-pone-0358039: A common stomach bug may raise the risk of gout. This large health-examination study explored Helicobacter pylori infection’s link to hyperuricemia and serum uric acid levels, through metabolic, renal, and inflammatory pathways. plos-pone-0341539: Road bases built from industrial waste must survive endless wet-dry cycles. The models tell engineers whether this waste-based material will hold up under real roads.
plos-pone-0355839: Destroying one inner ear triggers a remarkable rewiring throughout the brain. This paper studied central and peripheral plasticity after chemical unilateral labyrinthectomy — tracking glial responses, calyx dynamics, and behavioral consequences. The findings map how the vestibular system recovers its balance after catastrophic loss.
plos-pone-0352239: Studying glioblastoma — the deadliest brain cancer — demands realistic lab models. The patterned platform gives researchers unprecedented control for experiments.
plos-pone-0355939: How well root canal motors shape the canal determines treatment success. This in vitro micro-CT study evaluated canal shaping extent using apex locator–integrated endodontic motors. The three-dimensional imaging comparison shows dentists which devices shape canals most faithfully.
plos-pone-0348339: Children who acquired HIV at birth and survived into adulthood — what becomes of their careers and education? This Bangkok study tracked career and education outcomes among perinatally infected people receiving care at two tertiary hospitals from 2014 to 2020. The life-course data reveal resilience and remaining gaps.
plos-pone-0356739: Zoonotic outbreaks — diseases jumping from animals to humans — need earlier warnings. This paper proposed an index-based system for early alerts of potential zoonotic disease outbreaks. The composite index synthesizes ecological and epidemiological signals, aiming to flag spillover risk before the first human case.
plos-pone-0356239: Hospitals must track antibiotic use carefully to fight resistance. This Jordanian study evaluated antibacterial agent use in adult patients at a tertiary-level hospital, comparing defined daily dose against days of therapy metrics. The comparative analysis reveals which measurement tells the truer story of prescribing — information stewardship programs need to curb misuse.
plos-pone-0356539: Hiring tests often screen out autistic candidates who’d excel at the job. This paper explored using selection tests to hire autistic employees — examining which methods work fairly. The findings point employers toward assessments that measure true ability rather than social performance.
plos-pone-0355739: Blast waves injure brains at the cellular level — altering mechanics and fate. This paper studied blast-induced traumatic brain injury’s effects on brain cellular mechanics and differentiation. The findings reveal how explosions reprogram brain cells — knowledge critical for protecting soldiers and blast victims.
plos-pone-0353139: The brain’s arithmetic networks were thought to shift with age — but maybe not. This registered report found no developmental fronto-parietal shift in brain activation during mental arithmetic across the lifespan. The null finding — pre-registered for credibility — challenges textbook accounts of numerical cognition.
europmc-pmc2860339: Sloppy trial reports waste science, so medicine built a checklist. This 2010 paper delivers the CONSORT 2010 Statement, updated rules for reporting randomized trials. europmc-pmc2941839: Old-school GC/MS still rules steroid detective work. This 2010 paper argues gas chromatography-mass spectrometry remains a top discovery tool in clinical steroid studies, even in the fast-LC era. The authors defend the veteran. Their case keeps a classic relevant.
europmc-pmc2943439: Medical evidence pours out faster than anyone can drink. This 2010 paper notes seventy-five trials and eleven systematic reviews appear daily, asking how we will ever keep up. The authors' famous count shocked the field. Their paper spurred smarter evidence synthesis.
europmc-pmc2991639: Short bursts of hard exercise burn fat fast. This 2011 review covers high-intensity interval exercise and fat loss. The author finds bursts beat steady slogging. Their review popularized interval training for busy people. Twenty minutes can top an hour of jogging.
europmc-pmc3018439: Research priorities need setting well. This 2010 paper offers a nine-point checklist for fair health research agendas. The authors guide funders toward good practice. europmc-pmc3022639: Young people face real barriers to mental health help. This 2010 review surveys what stops and what helps youth seek care. The authors map stigma, cost, and access gaps. europmc-pmc3038139: Protein pH behavior got visual. This 2011 paper draws charts of how proteins act across acid and base. The authors' plots reveal the chemistry plainly. Their tool aids protein engineers. Drug designers pick stable pH ranges with it. The charts beat tables of raw numbers.
europmc-pmc3057439: Stubborn migraine met nerve zaps. This 2011 trial tests zapping the occipital nerve for chronic migraine that resists drugs. The authors' ONSTIM study shows promise. europmc-pmc3071839: A Parkinson's mutation wrecks mouse neurons. This 2011 paper shows mutant LRRK2 thins neurons, prunes their branches, and jams cleanup in mice. The authors model the disease. europmc-pmc3080339: Smartphones entered healthcare. This 2011 overview shows how phones enable mobile, participatory care, with eCAALYX as example. The authors chart the shift. europmc-pmc6534539: Human papillomavirus is known for causing cancer with its linear genes - but it also makes circular RNAs, and one of them packs a punch. europmc-pmc6598639: Suicide remains a leading killer worldwide, but its patterns vary sharply by place, age, and sex. europmc-pmc6599339: Systematic reviews live or die by how studies are picked - traditionally by two independent screeners. europmc-pmc6614039: HDX-MS watches proteins breathe: tracking how hydrogen atoms swap with deuterium reveals which parts of a protein are exposed or tucked away. europmc-pmc6639939: Liver cancer has a new suspect: circRHOT1, a circular RNA that cranks up the NR2F6 gene to drive tumor growth. This study traces the loop from rogue RNA to cancer progression in hepatocellular carcinoma. Silencing the circle could become a liver-cancer therapy.
europmc-pmc6650939: Radiation does not just kill cancer cells - it remodels their neighborhood. europmc-pmc6722139: Tumor-associated macrophages usually aid the enemy - but they can be reprogrammed. europmc-pmc6777939: Retinas cannot be biopsied - so researchers build them. Merging organoids with organ-on-a-chip tech, this study created layered human retina models to study blinding diseases like macular degeneration. The mini-retinas offer a testbed for therapies that eyes cannot spare.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-839: Iraq's oil money moved through Pentagon deals in 2007 — and GAO's report says the contracting rules got bent.
